_comment: Catalog for the Stage 2 review window (stage2-review.html).
AUTHORED data, not generated. Adding a Stage 2 type to the review window is an edit to this
file: give it a `banks` map (arm -> jsonl path) and, if a figure inspector exists for it, an
`inspector` id. build-stage2-review.mjs loads whichever bank files are actually present and
downgrades `status` to `designed` for any type whose banks are missing, so a designed-only type
still appears in the window with its intended shape rather than being omitted.
Every `designed` entry's text is a summary of docs/product/STAGE2_QUESTION_DESIGN.md section
`designSection`. That document's own status line is 'Nothing here is built' — the FLU-OPCHAIN-01
banks were built afterwards, and nothing is gated (Gate B needs ~128 real children).

types.name: Machine Chain
types.hiddenSystem: A badge to operator mapping. Six operators — turn, flip, slant (orientation, non-commuting) and swap, ring, twin (attribute toggles) — labelled by six arbitrary badge symbols. The mapping is what persists; the figures never repeat.
induces: which transform each badge stands for (the vocabulary)
that badges compose in badge order, left to right — the deep one, and what any depth ≥ 2 item requires
ladder: depth 1 — know what one badge does
depth 2 — chain two, in the right order
depth 3–4 — chain three or four, holding an imagined intermediate figure through steps that do not touch it
levers: composition depth, 1–4 (dominates: it is the ladder the learnable thing unlocks)
count of distinct orientation operators, which is where order starts to matter
representational mixing — a chain that interleaves orientation changes with attribute toggles
distractor distance along a named-failure axis (order error, applied twice, omission, wrong operator, first step only, identity copy)
types.notes: Bank status is gate-ready and ungated: 234 items per arm, born synthetic, syntheticOnly true and validated false. `difficulty` is a design rung computed from the levers, not a calibrated IRT parameter. Not wired into the live learning block.

types.name: Transform Machine
types.hiddenSystem: A machine that applies hidden spatial transformations to a block figure, drawn from a candidate set fixed for the whole block.
induces: which transformation the machine applies — the learnable thing is the rule, not rotation speed
how transformations chain, and that order matters
holding the intermediate figure in working memory
ladder: longer chains, and chains never demonstrated
levers: number of candidate transformations in play
whether the queried face is visible
distractor distance by named error, e.g. wrong axis
types.notes: Second in build order and called the biggest hole in the Stage 2 pool. It also carries the highest prior probability of failing its own scrambled control, because rotation practice is the most plausible source of a climb with no system in it — so the control is not optional here. Accuracy is scored; response time is never allowed into λ.

types.name: Alien Numbers
types.hiddenSystem: An invented numeral system: three or four glyphs, a hidden composition rule, base 3 or base 4, fixed for the block.
induces: the composition rule — sign-value or place-value
ladder: combine two under an additive rule
levers: number of glyphs in the expression
composition type — additive is established as easier than multiplicative
types.notes: Third in build order and has the best-evidenced difficulty structure of the four, because the composition orderings come from published work. Its open assumption is that adult orderings hold in children. Concreteness fading is designed in: glyph beside quantity at first, glyph alone by a fixed trial.

types.name: Word Machines
types.hiddenSystem: A tiny invented morphology: pseudo-syllable stems plus affixes carrying negation, plurality, size and agent or patient. Latin script, no audio.
induces: how morphemes combine — affix order, stacking, doubling
ladder: minimal pairs differing in one morpheme
types.notes: Built last, and the design its own author is least confident in: the open assumption is that it loads verbal rather than fluid reasoning, which would break comparability with a block that must stay in one area. Recommended for grade bands 2-3 and up, because at K-1 it largely measures decoding.
